h1: The 7 Best Mattress Vacuums Under $150, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mattress Vacuum Under $150: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 mattress vacuums under $150, compared on kPa suction, UV-C, heat, HEPA filtration, weight and price tier.
summary: The uwant 18Kpa is the best mattress vacuum under $150 for pure suction, while the FEPPO PRO is the best all-round pick with UV-C and four functions. The heated unit with a dust sensor is the best value for pet owners, and the 1.2kg 13Kpa model is the easiest to hold.
intro: Mattress vacuums sell on a handful of numbers, and the biggest one is easy to misread. Kilopascals describe how hard the motor pulls, not how much dust ends up in the bin, and a unit with a high figure and a weak filter can still leave a cloud of fine dust hanging over your bed. Add a UV-C lamp and the marketing gets louder than the cleaning.

We ranked seven units, all well under $150, by suction, filtration, extra features and weight, using listing data. UV-C and heat claims come from the sellers, so we treat them as extras rather than reasons to buy. Suction and filtering decide whether a mattress actually gets cleaner.

products.name: uwant 18Kpa Mattress Vacuum
products.verdict: The only listing here that names 18Kpa suction, paired with a 60,000 RPM motor.
products.description:
The uwant is a handheld bed vacuum that lists 18Kpa of suction and a 60,000 RPM motor, the two highest figures in this ranking. Street pricing runs $50 to $100, and it targets people who put suction ahead of everything.

Kilopascals measure how hard the motor can pull air, and deep mattress fibers hold dust that light suction skims past. That is why 18Kpa ranks above the 16Kpa group, though the gap is two units, not a different class. Against the Teant and FEPPO units, uwant gives no UV-C or heat feature in our data, so you are paying for pull alone.

Buy it for a thick mattress or a pet-heavy bed. A high-RPM motor is also louder and drains a battery faster, and the listing publishes no runtime or weight, so check both before you commit.
products.idealFor: Buyers with thick mattresses who want maximum pull.
products.skipIf: You want sanitizing features in the same unit.

products.name: FEPPO Mattress Vacuum Cleaner PRO 4-in-1
products.verdict: 16Kpa suction with UV-C light and a four-function design in one body.
products.description:
The FEPPO PRO is a 4-in-1 bed vacuum with 16Kpa suction and UV-C light, in the $50 to $100 bucket. The multi-function label signals extra modes beyond straight vacuuming.

It ranks second because the combination is the most complete: strong suction plus a built-in UV lamp. The uwant beats it on raw pull by 2Kpa, but FEPPO covers more jobs. UV-C on a vacuum acts only where the lamp sits close to the fabric, so treat it as a bonus on top of suction, never a replacement for it.

It suits people who want one device for bedding, sofas and cushions. The listing does not break out the four functions, so check what the attachments do before buying.
products.idealFor: Households wanting one tool for beds and upholstery.
products.skipIf: You want the absolute strongest suction.

products.name: Heated UV-C Mattress Vacuum with 149°F Heat
products.verdict: Adds 149°F heat and a smart dust sensor to 16Kpa suction at the low price tier.
products.description:
This unnamed-brand unit pairs 16Kpa suction with a 275nm UV-C light, a 149°F heating function and a smart dust sensor, marketed for pet hair and dander. It sits in the $25 to $50 range.

It places third because it carries the longest feature list at the lowest cost. Heat can help dry out damp bedding and loosen debris, and the dust sensor reports how dirty a pass is, which tells you when to stop. Against the FEPPO PRO it trades name recognition for a lower price.

Buy it for a pet bed or a shedding dog on the duvet. The caution is verification: UV-C and heat claims come from the listing, so use them as extras and rely on suction to do the real cleaning.
products.idealFor: Pet owners who want heat, light and suction cheaply.
products.skipIf: You want a recognized brand's support.

products.name: Cordless 16Kpa Mattress Vacuum with HEPA
products.verdict: Cordless with UV-C, HEPA and ultrasonic features at a low price.
products.description:
This cordless handheld lists 16Kpa suction, a 253.7nm UV-C lamp, a HEPA filter and an ultrasonic feature, in the $25 to $50 tier.

It sits fourth because the HEPA filter is the spec that matters for allergy sufferers, since a vacuum without sealed filtration can blow fine dust back into the room. The ultrasonic feature is marketed to loosen mites, but the listing gives no detail on how, so we rate it as a bonus only.

It suits people who vacuum a bed weekly and do not want to chase a cord. Battery capacity and runtime are not published, so look at owner feedback before relying on one charge for a king-size bed.
products.idealFor: Allergy-conscious buyers who want a cordless bed vacuum.

products.name: Teant 16 kPa UV-C Mattress Vacuum
products.verdict: A 16 kPa unit with a stated 253.7nm UV-C light, but at the top of the price range.
products.description:
The Teant lists 16 kPa suction and a 253.7nm UV-C light, in the $50 to $100 bracket, which our data marks as the highest-priced confirmed listing in the category.

It ranks fifth since you pay more for the same 16Kpa and UV-C pairing the FEPPO PRO already carries, minus the 4-in-1 function. The 253.7nm figure is the standard germicidal UV-C wavelength, which at least shows the lamp specification was written down.

Buy it for a branded mid-tier option. The caveat is that nothing here beats the cheaper heated unit on features, so choose it on availability or return policy, not specs.
products.idealFor: Shoppers who want a branded 16 kPa UV-C option.
products.skipIf: You compare units on features per dollar.

products.name: CFBF Mattress Bed Vacuum with UV-C
products.verdict: Core 16Kpa suction and UV-C at the $25 to $50 tier, nothing extra.
products.description:
The CFBF bed vacuum keeps it simple, with 16Kpa suction and a 253.7nm UV-C light in the $25 to $50 range.

It sits sixth because the specs match the cheaper heated unit and the HEPA model but carry no extras. Against the cordless HEPA model it has no documented filtration, and against the heated unit it offers no dust sensor or heat, so it matches rivals on suction without winning on anything else.

Buy it when you want bare suction with a sanitizing lamp and nothing else. The weakness is the lack of any documented filter, so if you have allergies pay a little more for the HEPA unit.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who only need suction and a lamp.
products.skipIf: You have allergies and want HEPA.

products.name: 13Kpa Lightweight Mattress Vacuum (1.2kg)
products.verdict: The lightest unit at 1.2kg, with LED headlights and heating, but 13Kpa suction.
products.description:
This model lists 13Kpa suction, UV-C light, LED headlights, a high heating technology and a weight of 1.2kg, in the $25 to $50 tier.

It ranks last on suction, 3Kpa below the 16Kpa group and 5Kpa below the uwant, and in this category pull is the number that matters most. The compensation is weight: 1.2kg is easy to hold overhead and carry up stairs, and the LED lights show dust on dark sheets that a plain unit would miss.

Buy it for a light mattress or a child's bed where comfort matters more than deep pull. Expect slower passes on a thick pillow-top.
products.idealFor: Light mattresses and users who want an easy-to-hold unit.
products.skipIf: You have a thick pillow-top mattress.

whatMatters.detail: Kilopascals rate how hard the motor pulls air, and deep mattress fibers hold dust that light suction skims past. Here 16Kpa is the common figure, the uwant reaches 18Kpa and the lightweight 1.2kg unit sits at 13Kpa. Compare the numbers, but remember sellers do not rate them uniformly. Look for a stated Kpa figure, and treat a missing one as a red flag.

A HEPA filter traps fine particles that ordinary filters push back into the room as exhaust, which is the exact thing allergy sufferers want to avoid when they vacuum a bed. Only the cordless 16Kpa model lists HEPA in this ranking. If filtration is your reason to buy, look for HEPA by name in the spec list, not a vague claim of strong filtering.

UV-C is short-wavelength light that can inactivate microbes, but only when it shines on a surface for long enough. A vacuum sweeps past each spot in a second or two, so the effect is limited. The 253.7nm lamp appears on the Teant, CFBF and cordless picks, and 275nm on the heated unit. Look for the wavelength stated, and rely on suction first.

Heat helps by loosening debris and drying damp fibers, but it is a supporting feature. The heated unit lists 149°F, which is mild compared with a steam or dryer cycle, and a heat claim says nothing about how long it runs or whether it reaches deep fibers. Check how the listing describes the heat, and do not pay extra for it alone.

You hold the unit at arm's length across a whole queen or king bed, so weight and cord decide how long you can stay at it. The 13Kpa model lists 1.2kg, but most listings give no figure, and the uwant's 60,000 RPM motor suggests a loud, battery-hungry unit. Look for a stated weight and runtime, or pick a cordless design.

faq.q: Will it work on any mattress?
faq.a: Yes on most, but thickness matters. The uwant's 18Kpa copes best with a deep pillow-top, where dust sits far below the surface, while the 13Kpa unit suits thinner or lighter beds. Match the suction number to how thick and dusty your mattress is.

Buying on UV-C alone. A passing lamp does little in the second it sits over each spot, so the 16Kpa suction on the FEPPO PRO or CFBF is what really cleans. Choose by suction and filter first, and treat the lamp as a small extra.

faq.q: Is a mattress vacuum worth it over a normal vacuum?
faq.a: If you have pets or allergies, yes. These units are lighter and sized for beds, and the cordless HEPA model also filters fine dust. A normal upright is clumsy on a mattress and often lacks a small, sealed filter. For a single guest bed, a standard vacuum may suffice.

Vacuum slowly in overlapping lines, and cover the whole bed in two or three passes, including the seams where dust collects. The heated unit's dust sensor tells you when a patch is clean. Slow passes matter more than speed because suction needs time to pull from deep fibers.

Empty the dust cup after each bed and tap the filter clean over a bin. On the HEPA unit, replace the filter on the maker's schedule, since a clogged filter drops suction. Keep the UV-C lamp window wiped so the light is not blocked.

faq.q: Does heat or UV-C kill everything?
faq.a: No. UV-C acts only where it lingers, and 149°F heat is modest. Wash sheets weekly and use suction for the real work. None of these listings promise sterilization, so do not rely on the FEPPO PRO or the heated unit as a disinfectant.

finalTake: The uwant 18Kpa is the suction leader and the FEPPO PRO the best all-rounder, while the heated unit gives pet owners the most features at the lowest cost. Choose HEPA if you have allergies, and ignore sanitizing claims as your reason to buy. Suction and filtration clean the bed, and everything else is a bonus.
